**Search efficiency depends on how many hyperparameters really matter.** In a two-dimensional grid with five values per axis, 25 trials explore only five distinct values of each parameter. Random search can explore 25 different values of an influential parameter while also varying the less important one. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/user_guide.html)

That explains why random search can outperform a grid when only a few dimensions strongly affect performance. A carefully designed grid can still be useful for a small, well-understood space.

Bayesian optimization uses previous results to choose promising trials; TPE models regions associated with good and bad outcomes. Hyperband and ASHA allocate more resources to promising trials and terminate weak ones early.

**Early performance must be informative.** A slow-starting learning-rate schedule may be pruned before it becomes strong. Define minimum budgets, failure handling, and consistent validation. Compare total compute, not just number of trials. Repeatedly searching one holdout also creates selection bias, so confirm the selected configuration independently. Search machinery cannot compensate for a leaked metric or an inappropriate parameter range.

**Technical details and references.**

Grid search spends combinations on every axis; if only a few hyperparameters matter, random search samples more distinct values along those influential axes for the same trial count. This is an assumption-dependent efficiency argument, not a universal theorem that random always wins. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/user_guide.html)

Bayesian optimization uses observed trials to choose promising configurations; TPE models good/bad parameter regions. Hyperband/ASHA allocate more resources to promising trials and stop weak ones early, improving throughput when early performance predicts final performance.

Slow-starting configurations can be pruned unfairly. Set reproducible budgets, validation splits, failure handling, and search spaces; compare total compute and best independently verified score. Avoid treating repeated evaluation on one holdout as unlimited free statistical evidence.
